The file ring-core/src/ring/util/io.clj has input-stream helpers (`piped-input-stream`, `string-input-stream`) but no output counterparts. Add three public stream helpers in the same style:
1. `string-output-stream` — returns a java.io.ByteArrayOutputStream containing the given String's bytes; two arities: [s] and [s encoding].
2. `piped-output-stream` — the output-stream twin of `piped-input-stream`: takes a function of an input stream, runs it in a separate thread on a piped input stream, and returns the connected output stream.
3. `close-all!` — takes a collection of streams and closes each one, swallowing exceptions, reusing the existing `close!`.

content.text:
(ns ring.util.io
  "Utility functions for handling I/O."
  (:import [java.io PipedInputStream
            PipedOutputStream
            ByteArrayInputStream
            File
            IOException]))

(defn piped-input-stream
  "Create an input stream from a function that takes an output stream as its
  argument. The function will be executed in a separate thread. The stream
  will be automatically closed after the function finishes.

  For example:

    (piped-input-stream
      (fn [ostream]
        (spit ostream \"Hello\")))"
  {:added "1.1"}
  [func]
  (let [input  (PipedInputStream.)
        output (PipedOutputStream.)]
    (.connect input output)
    (future
      (try
        (func output)
        (finally (.close output))))
    input))

(defn string-input-stream
  "Returns a ByteArrayInputStream for the given String."
  {:added "1.1"}
  ([^String s]
   (ByteArrayInputStream. (.getBytes s)))
  ([^String s ^String encoding]
   (ByteArrayInputStream. (.getBytes s encoding))))

(defn close!
  "Ensure a stream is closed, swallowing any exceptions."
  {:added "1.2"}
  [stream]
  (when (instance? java.io.Closeable stream)
    (try
      (.close ^java.io.Closeable stream)
      (catch IOException _ nil))))

(defn last-modified-date
  "Returns the last modified date for a file, rounded down to the nearest
  second."
  {:added "1.2"}
  [^File file]
  (-> (.lastModified file)
      (/ 1000) (long) (* 1000)
      (java.util.Date.)))

content.text:
Done. Added to `ring-core/src/ring/util/io.clj`:

1. **`string-output-stream`** — two arities `([s])` / `([s encoding])`, returning a `ByteArrayOutputStream`. Note: I initially used the `ByteArrayOutputStream. (.getBytes s)` constructor form, but that fails at runtime (`ByteArrayOutputStream`'s only single-arg constructor is `(int)` — the compiler dispatches to it and throws a `ClassCastException` on the `byte[]`). Fixed by constructing empty and calling `.write`.
2. **`piped-output-stream`** — exact twin of `piped-input-stream`: connects a `PipedInputStream`/`PipedOutputStream` pair, runs `func` over the *input* stream in a `future` that closes it in a `finally`, and returns the connected *output* stream. `{:added "1.2"}`, docstring with an example, matching the existing style.
3. **`close-all!`** — `doseq` over a collection of streams, delegating to the existing `close!` (which swallows exceptions).

Also added `ByteArrayOutputStream` to the `java.io` `:import` list.

Verified: file parses (8 forms, guard report clean), the ns loads, and a smoke test confirmed round-trips for all three (`string-output-stream` with default and `UTF-8` encoding, `piped-output-stream` delivering written bytes to the consumer thread, and `close-all!` closing the stream without error).
